newsitem.title: GERMANY: German panel debates details of pension reform.
newsitem.headline: German panel debates details of pension reform.

text.p: Pension policy experts from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) on Sunday discussed Labour Minister Norbert Bluem's reform plan, which won broad support at the weekend after initial strife.

The need to restructure Germany's pay-as-you-go public pension system sparked open warfare within Kohl's coalition, pitting Bluem's hopes for greater tax support for public programmes against Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plans to levy taxes on pensions.

Kohl publicly berated Bluem -- the longest-serving member of his cabinet -- for breaking ranks. His junior coalition partners in the Free Democrat Party (FDP) have also been vocal in criticising Bluem.

But on Saturday policy gurus from Kohl's CDU and its sister party, the Bavaria-based Christian Social Union led by Waigel, quietly united in basic support of Bluem's plan after an eight-hour negotiating session.
"The CDU and CSU are standing side by side," Bluem said after Saturday's session in Frankfurt. "It is a good day."

Younger parliamentarians, reflecting their generation's concern that the system will be broke by the time they reach retirement, have proposed building up its capital reserves in a fund that could not be hijacked for other purposes.
While technocrats hash out the details, they know that the ultimate solution of the crisis can only be reached at the top political level.
"I have seen that Bluem can fight, and he is doing it here," said one CDU parliamentarian.

Topping the agenda for Sunday's meeting was a discussion of Bluem's plans for a tax-supported "Family Fund", which would take over part of the non-insurance outlays now paid by the social insurance system.
Bluem's pension reform plan would cut pensions to 64 percent of average income by 2030 from 70 percent now.
It would also cut pension premiums to 18.7 percent of wages by 2010 from 20.3 percent currently, but raise it to 22.9 percent later.
